I used OpenAI Codex to assist with translating the assignment requirements into

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(readr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(glmnet)
  library(mgcv)
  library(ranger)
  library(pROC)
  library(knitr)
})

here::i_am("checkpoint2.qmd")
set.seed(70702)

data_dir     <- here::here("data")
set_a_dir    <- here::here("data", "set-a")
outcomes_csv <- here::here("data", "Outcomes-a.txt")
out_dir      <- here::here("output")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

expected_n <- 4000L
outer_k <- 5L
inner_k <- 3L
rare_measurement_threshold <- 0.10
lambda_grid <- 10^seq(0, -4, length.out = 30)
rf_num_trees <- 250L

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
)
```

# 2.1 Modeling table

Checkpoint 2 uses **set-a only**. The modeling table has one row per ICU stay,
so no stay can appear in both training and validation within a fold. Repeated
measurements are summarized over hours 0--48. The binary outcome is
in-hospital death from `Outcomes-a.txt`.

The data are from the PhysioNet/Computing in Cardiology Challenge 2012,
“Predicting Mortality of ICU Patients” (Silva, Moody, Scott, Celi, and Mark,
2012), released under the Open Data Commons Attribution License. The dataset
and its attribution information are available from
[PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2012/1.0.0/), and the study
description is available from
[PubMed Central](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3965265/).

```{r}
#| label: check-and-load-data

if (!dir.exists(set_a_dir)) stop("Missing data/set-a/")
if (!file.exists(outcomes_csv)) stop("Missing data/Outcomes-a.txt")

set_a_files <- sort(list.files(
  set_a_dir,
  pattern = "^[0-9]+\\.txt$",
  full.names = TRUE
))

if (length(set_a_files) != expected_n) {
  stop("Expected 4000 set-a files; found ", length(set_a_files))
}

time_to_minutes <- function(x) {
  parts <- strsplit(x, ":", fixed = TRUE)
  vapply(parts, function(z) {
    if (length(z) != 2L) return(NA_real_)
    60 * as.numeric(z[[1]]) + as.numeric(z[[2]])
  }, numeric(1))
}

load_one_record <- function(path) {
  file_id <- as.integer(sub("\\.txt$", "", basename(path)))
  x <- data.table::fread(path, showProgress = FALSE)
  names(x) <- trimws(names(x))
  stopifnot(all(c("Time", "Parameter", "Value") %in% names(x)))
  x[, Parameter := trimws(as.character(Parameter))]
  x[, Time := trimws(as.character(Time))]
  x[, Value := as.numeric(Value)]

  embedded_id <- x[Parameter == "RecordID", Value]
  if (length(embedded_id) != 1L || as.integer(embedded_id[[1]]) != file_id) {
    stop("RecordID does not match filename: ", path)
  }

  x <- x[Parameter != "RecordID"]
  x[, RecordID := file_id]
  x[, .(
    RecordID,
    Time,
    Minutes = time_to_minutes(Time),
    Parameter,
    Value_raw = Value
  )]
}

long_raw <- data.table::rbindlist(
  lapply(set_a_files, load_one_record),
  use.names = TRUE
) |>
  as_tibble()

if (anyNA(long_raw$Minutes)) stop("At least one Time value could not be parsed")

outcomes <- readr::read_csv(
  outcomes_csv,
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
names(outcomes) <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", names(outcomes))
names(outcomes) <- gsub("_+$", "", names(outcomes))

required_outcomes <- c(
  "RecordID", "SAPS_I", "SOFA", "Length_of_stay",
  "Survival", "In_hospital_death"
)
if (!all(required_outcomes %in% names(outcomes))) {
  stop("Unexpected Outcomes-a.txt columns")
}

outcomes <- outcomes |>
  mutate(
    RecordID = as.integer(RecordID),
    In_hospital_death = as.integer(In_hospital_death)
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(outcomes) == expected_n,
  !anyDuplicated(outcomes$RecordID),
  setequal(long_raw$RecordID, outcomes$RecordID),
  all(outcomes$In_hospital_death %in% c(0L, 1L))
)
```

The cleaning rules carry forward the Checkpoint 1 decisions. The sentinel
value -1 is treated as missing. Zero or clearly impossible height and weight
values and selected measurements outside deliberately broad data-quality
bounds are retained in the raw column but excluded from model summaries. These
bounds are screens for obvious data problems, not clinical reference ranges.

```{r}
#| label: clean-data

quality_bounds <- tribble(
  ~Parameter,    ~lower, ~upper,
  "Age",             0,    130,
  "Gender",          0,      1,
  "Height",         50,    250,
  "ICUType",         1,      4,
  "Weight",         20,    400,
  "Albumin",         0,     20,
  "ALP",             0,   5000,
  "ALT",             0,  20000,
  "AST",             0,  20000,
  "Bilirubin",       0,    100,
  "BUN",             0,    300,
  "Cholesterol",     0,   1000,
  "Creatinine",      0,     30,
  "DiasABP",         0,    250,
  "FiO2",            0,      1,
  "GCS",             3,     15,
  "Glucose",         0,   2000,
  "HCO3",            0,    100,
  "HCT",             0,    100,
  "HR",              0,    300,
  "K",               0,     15,
  "Lactate",         0,     40,
  "MAP",             0,    250,
  "MechVent",        0,      1,
  "Mg",              0,     20,
  "Na",             80,    220,
  "NIDiasABP",       0,    250,
  "NIMAP",           0,    250,
  "NISysABP",        0,    300,
  "PaCO2",           0,    300,
  "PaO2",            0,    800,
  "pH",              0,     14,
  "Platelets",       0,   2000,
  "RespRate",        0,    100,
  "SaO2",            0,    100,
  "SysABP",          0,    300,
  "Temp",           25,     45,
  "TroponinI",       0,   1000,
  "TroponinT",       0,   1000,
  "Urine",           0,  10000,
  "WBC",             0,    500
)

long <- long_raw |>
  left_join(quality_bounds, by = "Parameter") |>
  mutate(
    Value = if_else(Value_raw == -1, NA_real_, Value_raw),
    implausible =
      !is.na(Value) & !is.na(lower) & !is.na(upper) &
      (Value < lower | Value > upper),
    Value_clean = if_else(implausible | !is.finite(Value), NA_real_, Value)
  ) |>
  arrange(RecordID, Minutes, Parameter)

first_nonmissing <- function(x) {
  y <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(y) == 0L) NA_real_ else y[[1]]
}

static_parameters <- c("Age", "Gender", "Height", "ICUType", "Weight")

static <- long |>
  filter(Parameter %in% static_parameters) |>
  group_by(RecordID, Parameter) |>
  summarise(Value = first_nonmissing(Value_clean), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = RecordID,
    names_from = Parameter,
    values_from = Value,
    names_repair = "check_unique"
  )

long_48 <- long |>
  filter(
    between(Minutes, 0, 48 * 60),
    !Parameter %in% static_parameters,
    !is.na(Value_clean)
  )

parameter_availability <- long_48 |>
  distinct(RecordID, Parameter) |>
  count(Parameter, name = "stays_measured") |>
  mutate(
    percent_measured = 100 * stays_measured / expected_n,
    keep = stays_measured / expected_n >= rare_measurement_threshold
  ) |>
  arrange(percent_measured)

kept_parameters <- parameter_availability |>
  filter(keep) |>
  pull(Parameter)

all_dynamic_parameters <- parameter_availability$Parameter

dropped_parameters <- parameter_availability |>
  filter(!keep) |>
  select(Parameter, stays_measured, percent_measured)
```

```{r}
#| label: create-modeling-table

slope_or_na <- function(time_minutes, value) {
  if (length(value) < 2L || n_distinct(time_minutes) < 2L) return(NA_real_)
  unname(coef(lm(value ~ I(time_minutes / 60)))[[2]])
}

dynamic_summary <- long_48 |>
  arrange(RecordID, Parameter, Minutes) |>
  group_by(RecordID, Parameter) |>
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    last = dplyr::last(Value_clean),
    min = min(Value_clean),
    max = max(Value_clean),
    mean = mean(Value_clean),
    slope = slope_or_na(Minutes, Value_clean),
    never = 0L,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = RecordID,
    names_from = Parameter,
    values_from = c(count, last, min, max, mean, slope, never),
    names_glue = "{Parameter}_{.value}",
    names_sort = TRUE,
    names_repair = "check_unique"
  )

count_columns <- grep("_count$", names(dynamic_summary), value = TRUE)
never_columns <- grep("_never$", names(dynamic_summary), value = TRUE)

dynamic_summary <- dynamic_summary |>
  mutate(
    across(all_of(count_columns), ~ replace_na(.x, 0)),
    across(all_of(never_columns), ~ replace_na(.x, 1))
  )

modeling_table <- outcomes |>
  select(
    RecordID, In_hospital_death, SAPS_I, SOFA,
    Length_of_stay, Survival
  ) |>
  left_join(static, by = "RecordID") |>
  left_join(dynamic_summary, by = "RecordID") |>
  arrange(RecordID)

stopifnot(
  nrow(modeling_table) == expected_n,
  !anyDuplicated(modeling_table$RecordID),
  all(modeling_table$In_hospital_death %in% c(0L, 1L))
)

cohort_summary <- modeling_table |>
  summarise(
    `ICU stays` = n(),
    Deaths = sum(In_hospital_death),
    `Deaths (%)` = round(100 * mean(In_hospital_death), 1)
  )

knitr::kable(cohort_summary, caption = "Checkpoint 2 modeling cohort")
```

The modeling table contains `r nrow(modeling_table)` unique ICU stays and
`r sum(modeling_table$In_hospital_death)` deaths
(`r sprintf('%.1f%%', 100 * mean(modeling_table$In_hospital_death))`).

# 2.2 Predictors

All predictors use information available by hour 48. `Length_of_stay` and
`Survival` are excluded because they occur after the prediction window.
`RecordID` is an identifier, and SAPS-I and SOFA are held out as benchmark
risk scores rather than supplied to any model. ICU type is represented with
separate indicator columns, not as a numeric 1--4 trend.

```{r}
#| label: predictor-table

predictor_group_table <- tibble(
  `Predictor group` = c(
    "Baseline continuous",
    "Baseline categorical",
    "Last observed value",
    "Minimum and maximum",
    "Mean",
    "Linear slope",
    "Measurement count",
    "Never-measured indicator"
  ),
  `Number before one-hot encoding` = c(
    3L, 2L,
    length(kept_parameters),
    2L * length(kept_parameters),
    length(kept_parameters),
    length(kept_parameters),
    length(kept_parameters),
    length(kept_parameters)
  ),
  `Clinical or modeling reason` = c(
    "Age, height, and initial weight describe baseline reserve and body size.",
    "Sex and ICU type capture broad patient and care-context differences.",
    "The latest value approximates physiologic state near the prediction time.",
    "Extremes capture instability that a mean can hide.",
    "The mean summarizes overall burden during the observation window.",
    "A slope captures improvement or deterioration over time.",
    "Monitoring intensity can encode severity and care decisions.",
    "Missingness itself may be informative in clinical data."
  )
)

predictor_group_table <- bind_rows(
  predictor_group_table,
  tibble(
    `Predictor group` = "Total before one-hot encoding",
    `Number before one-hot encoding` =
      sum(predictor_group_table$`Number before one-hot encoding`),
    `Clinical or modeling reason` =
      "Total across all prespecified predictor groups."
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  predictor_group_table,
  caption = paste(
    "Predictor groups for the final all-set-a refit;", length(kept_parameters),
    "longitudinal variables passed the availability threshold"
  )
)
```

The table shows that the design combines physiologic level, extremes, trend,
and measurement behavior rather than relying on a single summary. Counts and
never-measured indicators explicitly retain clinically informative missingness.

Variables measured in fewer than
`r sprintf('%.0f%%', 100 * rare_measurement_threshold)` of stays are excluded
from a fitted model because their numerical summaries would be almost entirely
imputed. To prevent information from a held-out fold affecting predictor
selection, this threshold is recalculated separately inside every outer and
inner training fold and then applied unchanged to that fold's validation data.
For the final model refit only, the threshold is calculated on all set-a; the
table below lists the variables excluded from that final refit.

```{r}
#| label: dropped-variables

if (nrow(dropped_parameters) == 0L) {
  dropped_display <- tibble(
    Parameter = "None",
    stays_measured = expected_n,
    percent_measured = 100
  )
} else {
  dropped_display <- dropped_parameters |>
    mutate(percent_measured = round(percent_measured, 1))
}

knitr::kable(
  dropped_display,
  caption = "Variables excluded from the final all-set-a refit for being measured in fewer than 10% of stays"
)
```

The table makes the availability rule auditable: listed variables are too
sparse for reliable numeric summaries in the final refit, while variables not
listed passed the stated 10% threshold. Fold-specific retained sets may differ
slightly because each cross-validation decision uses training stays only.

```{r}
#| label: fixed-domain-encoding

# Fixed, clinically defined levels avoid learning category meanings from the
# full data. Missing static fields receive explicit indicators and are then
# median-imputed inside each training fold.
design_table <- modeling_table |>
  mutate(
    Age_missing = as.integer(is.na(Age)),
    Height_missing = as.integer(is.na(Height)),
    Weight_missing = as.integer(is.na(Weight)),
    Gender_Male = if_else(is.na(Gender), NA_real_, as.numeric(Gender == 1)),
    Gender_missing = as.integer(is.na(Gender)),
    ICUType_1_CCU = as.numeric(ICUType == 1),
    ICUType_2_CSRU = as.numeric(ICUType == 2),
    ICUType_3_MICU = as.numeric(ICUType == 3),
    ICUType_4_SICU = as.numeric(ICUType == 4),
    ICUType_missing = as.integer(is.na(ICUType))
  ) |>
  select(-Gender, -ICUType)

excluded_columns <- c(
  "RecordID", "In_hospital_death", "SAPS_I", "SOFA",
  "Length_of_stay", "Survival"
)
predictor_columns <- setdiff(names(design_table), excluded_columns)
x_raw <- as.data.frame(design_table[predictor_columns])
y <- design_table$In_hospital_death

stopifnot(
  !any(c("RecordID", "SAPS_I", "SOFA", "Length_of_stay", "Survival") %in%
         names(x_raw)),
  all(vapply(x_raw, is.numeric, logical(1)))
)
```

After fixed one-hot encoding and explicit indicators for missing baseline
fields, the candidate LASSO and random-forest design matrix contains
`r ncol(x_raw)` columns before fold-specific availability filtering.

# 2.3 Cross-validation design

I use stratified 5-fold cross-validation (CV), with the same fold assignment
for every model and benchmark. Each outer validation fold is untouched until
the selected configuration is evaluated. Within every outer training fold,
missing values are imputed from that training fold only; LASSO predictors are
also centered and scaled using training-fold values only. The 10% measurement-
availability screen is fitted inside each training fold, including each inner
fold, and only that training-derived column set is applied to validation data.
Hyperparameters are selected with an additional stratified 3-fold CV inside
the outer training fold. Thus the reported outer-fold AUROCs are not used to
tune the models or select predictors.

```{r}
#| label: cv-helpers

make_stratified_folds <- function(y, k, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  fold <- integer(length(y))
  for (class_value in sort(unique(y))) {
    idx <- sample(which(y == class_value))
    fold[idx] <- rep(seq_len(k), length.out = length(idx))
  }
  fold
}

dynamic_summary_suffixes <- c(
  "count", "last", "min", "max", "mean", "slope", "never"
)

dynamic_feature_names <- as.vector(outer(
  all_dynamic_parameters,
  dynamic_summary_suffixes,
  paste,
  sep = "_"
))

select_training_predictors <- function(x) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x)
  retained_parameters <- all_dynamic_parameters[vapply(
    all_dynamic_parameters,
    function(parameter) {
      count_name <- paste0(parameter, "_count")
      count_name %in% names(x) &&
        mean(replace_na(x[[count_name]], 0) > 0) >=
          rare_measurement_threshold
    },
    logical(1)
  )]

  retained_dynamic <- as.vector(outer(
    retained_parameters,
    dynamic_summary_suffixes,
    paste,
    sep = "_"
  ))

  static_columns <- setdiff(names(x), dynamic_feature_names)
  unique(c(static_columns, intersect(retained_dynamic, names(x))))
}

fit_preprocessor <- function(x, scale = TRUE) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x)
  medians <- vapply(x, function(z) {
    if (all(is.na(z))) 0 else median(z, na.rm = TRUE)
  }, numeric(1))

  imputed <- x
  for (nm in names(imputed)) {
    imputed[[nm]][is.na(imputed[[nm]])] <- medians[[nm]]
  }

  sds <- vapply(imputed, sd, numeric(1))
  keep <- names(sds)[is.finite(sds) & sds > 0]
  imputed <- imputed[keep]
  centers <- vapply(imputed, mean, numeric(1))
  scales <- vapply(imputed, sd, numeric(1))

  list(
    medians = medians,
    keep = keep,
    centers = centers,
    scales = scales,
    scale = scale
  )
}

apply_preprocessor <- function(prep, x) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x)
  x <- x[names(prep$medians)]
  for (nm in names(x)) {
    x[[nm]][is.na(x[[nm]])] <- prep$medians[[nm]]
  }
  x <- x[prep$keep]
  if (prep$scale) {
    x <- sweep(as.matrix(x), 2, prep$centers, "-")
    x <- sweep(x, 2, prep$scales, "/")
    return(x)
  }
  as.data.frame(x)
}

safe_auc <- function(truth, score) {
  ok <- is.finite(score) & !is.na(truth)
  if (length(unique(truth[ok])) < 2L) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(pROC::auc(pROC::roc(
    response = truth[ok],
    predictor = score[ok],
    levels = c(0, 1),
    direction = "<",
    quiet = TRUE
  )))
}

outer_fold <- make_stratified_folds(y, outer_k, seed = 70702)

fold_balance <- tibble(
  Fold = outer_fold,
  Death = y
) |>
  group_by(Fold) |>
  summarise(
    Stays = n(),
    Deaths = sum(Death),
    `Death rate (%)` = round(100 * mean(Death), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(fold_balance, caption = "Shared stratified outer folds")
```

The fold-balance table shows nearly identical numbers of stays and deaths in
each held-out fold, so model comparisons are not driven by different outcome
prevalence or different patient splits.

# 2.4 Model 1: LASSO logistic regression

I use least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic
regression. LASSO is appropriate here because the feature table is wide and
contains correlated summaries of the same physiologic signals. The L1 penalty
shrinks weak coefficients to zero, providing both regularization and a compact
model. All inputs are placed on a common scale within each training fold.

```{r}
#| label: lasso-functions

tune_lasso <- function(x, y, inner_fold, lambdas) {
  oof <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(x), ncol = length(lambdas))

  for (j in sort(unique(inner_fold))) {
    tr <- inner_fold != j
    va <- inner_fold == j
    inner_keep <- select_training_predictors(x[tr, , drop = FALSE])
    prep <- fit_preprocessor(
      x[tr, inner_keep, drop = FALSE],
      scale = TRUE
    )
    x_tr <- apply_preprocessor(
      prep,
      x[tr, inner_keep, drop = FALSE]
    )
    x_va <- apply_preprocessor(
      prep,
      x[va, inner_keep, drop = FALSE]
    )

    fit <- glmnet::glmnet(
      x = x_tr,
      y = y[tr],
      family = "binomial",
      alpha = 1,
      lambda = lambdas,
      standardize = FALSE
    )

    oof[va, ] <- as.matrix(predict(
      fit,
      newx = x_va,
      type = "response",
      s = lambdas
    ))
  }

  aucs <- vapply(seq_along(lambdas), function(i) {
    safe_auc(y, oof[, i])
  }, numeric(1))

  best <- which.max(aucs)
  list(lambda = lambdas[[best]], auc = aucs[[best]], all_auc = aucs)
}

fit_lasso_outer <- function(x_train, y_train, x_test, fold_number) {
  inner_fold <- make_stratified_folds(
    y_train,
    inner_k,
    seed = 72000 + fold_number
  )
  tuning <- tune_lasso(x_train, y_train, inner_fold, lambda_grid)
  outer_keep <- select_training_predictors(x_train)
  prep <- fit_preprocessor(x_train[outer_keep], scale = TRUE)
  x_tr <- apply_preprocessor(prep, x_train[outer_keep])
  x_te <- apply_preprocessor(prep, x_test[outer_keep])
  fit <- glmnet::glmnet(
    x_tr, y_train,
    family = "binomial",
    alpha = 1,
    lambda = tuning$lambda,
    standardize = FALSE
  )
  prediction <- as.numeric(predict(
    fit, newx = x_te, type = "response", s = tuning$lambda
  ))
  beta <- as.matrix(coef(fit, s = tuning$lambda))[, 1]
  selected <- setdiff(names(beta)[beta != 0], "(Intercept)")
  list(
    prediction = prediction,
    fit = fit,
    prep = prep,
    lambda = tuning$lambda,
    selected = selected,
    n_predictors = ncol(x_tr)
  )
}
```

The inner search evaluates 30 penalty values from
`r format(min(lambda_grid), scientific = TRUE)` to
`r format(max(lambda_grid), scientific = TRUE)`.

# 2.5 Model 2: generalized additive model

The generalized additive model (GAM) uses 14 clinically selected continuous
summaries rather than the full feature set. They cover baseline risk,
circulation, respiration, neurologic status, renal/metabolic function,
inflammation, and urine output. Cubic regression splines with four basis
functions allow modest non-linearity while limiting overfitting. Missingness
indicators and ICU-type indicators enter linearly. Smoothing penalties are
estimated by restricted maximum likelihood (REML) within each training fold.

```{r}
#| label: gam-functions

gam_continuous_candidates <- c(
  "Age", "Weight", "HR_mean", "Temp_mean", "MAP_mean",
  "RespRate_mean", "GCS_last", "Creatinine_mean", "BUN_mean",
  "Glucose_mean", "Lactate_mean", "WBC_mean", "Platelets_mean",
  "Urine_mean"
)

gam_linear_candidates <- c(
  "Gender_Male", "Gender_missing",
  "ICUType_1_CCU", "ICUType_2_CSRU", "ICUType_3_MICU",
  "ICUType_4_SICU", "ICUType_missing",
  "Lactate_never", "Urine_never", "GCS_never",
  "Lactate_count", "Urine_count"
)

gam_continuous <- intersect(gam_continuous_candidates, names(x_raw))
gam_linear <- intersect(gam_linear_candidates, names(x_raw))
gam_features <- unique(c(gam_continuous, gam_linear))

if (length(gam_continuous) < 10L) {
  stop("Too few prespecified GAM continuous predictors are available")
}

make_gam_formula <- function(continuous, linear) {
  smooth_terms <- paste0("s(", continuous, ", k = 4, bs = 'cr')")
  rhs <- paste(c(smooth_terms, linear), collapse = " + ")
  as.formula(paste("outcome ~", rhs))
}

fit_gam_outer <- function(x_train, y_train, x_test) {
  training_keep <- select_training_predictors(x_train)
  fold_features <- intersect(gam_features, training_keep)
  x_train <- x_train[fold_features]
  x_test <- x_test[fold_features]
  prep <- fit_preprocessor(x_train, scale = FALSE)
  tr <- apply_preprocessor(prep, x_train)
  te <- apply_preprocessor(prep, x_test)
  continuous_used <- intersect(gam_continuous, names(tr))
  linear_used <- intersect(gam_linear, names(tr))
  if (length(continuous_used) < 10L) {
    stop("Fewer than 10 prespecified GAM predictors passed the training-fold availability rule")
  }
  fold_gam_formula <- make_gam_formula(continuous_used, linear_used)
  train_data <- data.frame(outcome = y_train, tr, check.names = FALSE)
  fit <- mgcv::gam(
    fold_gam_formula,
    data = train_data,
    family = binomial(),
    method = "REML",
    select = TRUE
  )
  prediction <- as.numeric(predict(
    fit,
    newdata = data.frame(te, check.names = FALSE),
    type = "response"
  ))
  list(
    prediction = prediction,
    fit = fit,
    prep = prep,
    n_predictors = ncol(tr)
  )
}

gam_selection_table <- tibble(
  Predictor = c(gam_continuous, gam_linear),
  Role = c(
    rep("Spline term", length(gam_continuous)),
    rep("Linear/context or missingness term", length(gam_linear))
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  gam_selection_table,
  caption = "Clinically prespecified predictors used in the GAM"
)
```

The table shows the deliberately smaller GAM specification: clinically central
continuous variables receive spline terms, while care context and selected
missingness measures enter linearly. This keeps the nonlinear model readable
while covering the main physiologic domains.

# 2.6 Model 3: random forest

The tree ensemble is a probability random forest. It uses the same full
predictor set as LASSO. Missing values are median-imputed within each training
fold because `ranger` does not use missingness natively in this specification;
explicit counts and never-measured indicators remain available to the model.
The number of trees is fixed at `r rf_num_trees`; inner CV searches three
feature-subsampling values and two minimum node sizes.

```{r}
#| label: random-forest-functions

make_rf_grid <- function(p) {
  mtry_values <- unique(pmax(1L, pmin(
    p,
    as.integer(round(c(sqrt(p), p / 10, p / 5)))
  )))
  expand.grid(
    mtry = mtry_values,
    min.node.size = c(5L, 20L),
    KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE
  )
}

fit_one_rf <- function(x, y, mtry, min_node, seed) {
  ranger::ranger(
    x = as.data.frame(x),
    y = factor(y, levels = c(0, 1)),
    probability = TRUE,
    num.trees = rf_num_trees,
    mtry = mtry,
    min.node.size = min_node,
    importance = "impurity",
    num.threads = 2,
    seed = seed
  )
}

tune_rf <- function(x, y, inner_fold, seed) {
  # The grid is defined from a training-only preprocessing fit solely to obtain
  # the number of nonconstant columns. Every inner fit below re-fits its own
  # availability filtering, imputation, and zero-variance removal.
  dimension_keep <- select_training_predictors(x)
  dimension_prep <- fit_preprocessor(
    x[dimension_keep],
    scale = FALSE
  )
  grid <- make_rf_grid(length(dimension_prep$keep))
  grid$inner_auc <- NA_real_

  for (g in seq_len(nrow(grid))) {
    inner_oof <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(x))
    for (j in sort(unique(inner_fold))) {
      tr <- inner_fold != j
      va <- inner_fold == j
      inner_keep <- select_training_predictors(x[tr, , drop = FALSE])
      prep <- fit_preprocessor(
        x[tr, inner_keep, drop = FALSE],
        scale = FALSE
      )
      x_tr <- apply_preprocessor(
        prep,
        x[tr, inner_keep, drop = FALSE]
      )
      x_va <- apply_preprocessor(
        prep,
        x[va, inner_keep, drop = FALSE]
      )
      mtry_value <- min(grid$mtry[[g]], ncol(x_tr))
      fit <- fit_one_rf(
        x_tr, y[tr], mtry_value, grid$min.node.size[[g]],
        seed = seed + 100 * g + j
      )
      inner_oof[va] <- predict(
        fit,
        data = as.data.frame(x_va)
      )$predictions[, "1"]
    }
    grid$inner_auc[[g]] <- safe_auc(y, inner_oof)
  }

  grid[which.max(grid$inner_auc), , drop = FALSE]
}

fit_rf_outer <- function(x_train, y_train, x_test, fold_number) {
  inner_fold <- make_stratified_folds(
    y_train,
    inner_k,
    seed = 73000 + fold_number
  )
  best <- tune_rf(x_train, y_train, inner_fold, seed = 74000 + fold_number)
  outer_keep <- select_training_predictors(x_train)
  prep <- fit_preprocessor(x_train[outer_keep], scale = FALSE)
  x_tr <- apply_preprocessor(prep, x_train[outer_keep])
  x_te <- apply_preprocessor(prep, x_test[outer_keep])
  fit <- fit_one_rf(
    x_tr, y_train,
    mtry = min(best$mtry[[1]], ncol(x_tr)),
    min_node = best$min.node.size[[1]],
    seed = 75000 + fold_number
  )
  prediction <- predict(
    fit,
    data = as.data.frame(x_te)
  )$predictions[, "1"]
  list(
    prediction = prediction,
    fit = fit,
    prep = prep,
    best = best,
    n_predictors = ncol(x_tr)
  )
}

rf_grid_display <- make_rf_grid(ncol(x_raw))
rf_grid_display$num.trees <- rf_num_trees
knitr::kable(
  rf_grid_display,
  caption = "Random-forest tuning grid (mtry is capped after fold-specific preprocessing)"
)
```

The grid varies both feature subsampling and terminal-node size while keeping
the search small enough for nested validation. Because selection is based only
on inner-training AUROC, the outer held-out fold remains an unbiased comparison
set.

# Fit all models on the shared outer folds

```{r}
#| label: outer-cv

oof_predictions <- tibble(
  RecordID = modeling_table$RecordID,
  truth = y,
  fold = outer_fold,
  LASSO = NA_real_,
  GAM = NA_real_,
  RandomForest = NA_real_,
  SAPS_I = modeling_table$SAPS_I,
  SOFA = modeling_table$SOFA
)

fold_metrics <- list()
lasso_selection <- list()
outer_tuning <- list()

for (fold_number in seq_len(outer_k)) {
  train_idx <- outer_fold != fold_number
  test_idx <- outer_fold == fold_number
  x_train <- x_raw[train_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  x_test <- x_raw[test_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  y_train <- y[train_idx]
  y_test <- y[test_idx]

  lasso_result <- fit_lasso_outer(
    x_train, y_train, x_test, fold_number
  )
  gam_result <- fit_gam_outer(x_train, y_train, x_test)
  rf_result <- fit_rf_outer(x_train, y_train, x_test, fold_number)

  oof_predictions$LASSO[test_idx] <- lasso_result$prediction
  oof_predictions$GAM[test_idx] <- gam_result$prediction
  oof_predictions$RandomForest[test_idx] <- rf_result$prediction

  fold_scores <- list(
    LASSO = lasso_result$prediction,
    GAM = gam_result$prediction,
    RandomForest = rf_result$prediction,
    SAPS_I = modeling_table$SAPS_I[test_idx],
    SOFA = modeling_table$SOFA[test_idx]
  )

  fold_metrics[[fold_number]] <- bind_rows(lapply(
    names(fold_scores),
    function(model_name) tibble(
      fold = fold_number,
      model = model_name,
      AUROC = safe_auc(y_test, fold_scores[[model_name]])
    )
  ))

  lasso_selection[[fold_number]] <- tibble(
    fold = fold_number,
    predictor = lasso_result$selected
  )

  outer_tuning[[fold_number]] <- tibble(
    fold = fold_number,
    lasso_predictors = lasso_result$n_predictors,
    lasso_lambda = lasso_result$lambda,
    gam_predictors = gam_result$n_predictors,
    rf_predictors = rf_result$n_predictors,
    rf_mtry = rf_result$best$mtry[[1]],
    rf_min_node_size = rf_result$best$min.node.size[[1]],
    rf_inner_AUROC = rf_result$best$inner_auc[[1]]
  )
}

fold_metrics <- bind_rows(fold_metrics)
lasso_selection <- bind_rows(lasso_selection)
outer_tuning <- bind_rows(outer_tuning)

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(oof_predictions[c("LASSO", "GAM", "RandomForest")]),
  nrow(fold_metrics) == outer_k * 5L
)

readr::write_csv(
  oof_predictions,
  file.path(out_dir, "cp2_oof_predictions.csv")
)

knitr::kable(
  outer_tuning |>
    mutate(
      lasso_lambda = signif(lasso_lambda, 3),
      rf_inner_AUROC = round(rf_inner_AUROC, 3)
    ),
  caption = "Hyperparameters selected inside each outer training fold"
)
```

This table confirms that predictor availability filtering and tuning were
repeated within each outer training set. Small differences in predictor counts
are expected because held-out stays never contribute to the 10% availability
decision; the selected penalty and random-forest settings also vary by fold.

# LASSO coefficient magnitude and stability

```{r}
#| label: final-lasso

full_inner_fold <- make_stratified_folds(y, outer_k, seed = 76001)
final_lasso_tuning <- tune_lasso(x_raw, y, full_inner_fold, lambda_grid)
final_training_keep <- select_training_predictors(x_raw)
final_lasso_prep <- fit_preprocessor(
  x_raw[final_training_keep],
  scale = TRUE
)
final_lasso_x <- apply_preprocessor(
  final_lasso_prep,
  x_raw[final_training_keep]
)
final_lasso_fit <- glmnet::glmnet(
  final_lasso_x, y,
  family = "binomial",
  alpha = 1,
  lambda = final_lasso_tuning$lambda,
  standardize = FALSE
)

final_lasso_beta <- as.matrix(coef(
  final_lasso_fit,
  s = final_lasso_tuning$lambda
))[, 1]

coefficient_table <- tibble(
  predictor = names(final_lasso_beta),
  coefficient = as.numeric(final_lasso_beta)
) |>
  filter(predictor != "(Intercept)", coefficient != 0) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(coefficient)))

stability_table <- lasso_selection |>
  count(predictor, name = "selected_folds") |>
  mutate(
    selection_percent = 100 * selected_folds / outer_k,
    selected_in_final = predictor %in% coefficient_table$predictor
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(selected_folds), desc(selected_in_final), predictor)
```

The all-set-a LASSO retained `r nrow(coefficient_table)` predictors. Across the
outer folds, `r sum(stability_table$selected_folds == outer_k)` predictors were
selected in all five fits. Features selected repeatedly are more stable signals;
features appearing in only one or two folds should not be interpreted as robust
clinical discoveries because correlated summaries can substitute for one
another.

```{r}
#| label: lasso-coefficient-plot
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Largest non-zero coefficients from the LASSO refit on all set-a. Predictors were standardized, so coefficient magnitudes are comparable."

coefficient_plot_data <- coefficient_table |>
  slice_head(n = 30L) |>
  mutate(predictor = factor(predictor, levels = rev(predictor)))

ggplot(coefficient_plot_data, aes(x = coefficient, y = predictor, fill = coefficient > 0)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#3B82A0", "#B84A62")) +
  labs(
    x = "Standardized log-odds coefficient",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Largest LASSO coefficients"
  )
```

The plot shows which standardized features contribute most strongly after
simultaneous shrinkage. Positive coefficients increase predicted mortality and
negative coefficients decrease it, conditional on the other retained features;
they are predictive associations, not causal effects.

```{r}
#| label: lasso-stability-table

knitr::kable(
  stability_table |>
    slice_head(n = 30L),
  caption = "Thirty most frequently selected LASSO predictors across outer folds"
)
```

The table complements the coefficient plot by showing reproducibility across
patient splits: predictors appearing in all or most folds are more stable than
those selected only once, although stability still does not imply causality.

# GAM partial effects

```{r}
#| label: final-gam-and-effects

final_gam_features <- intersect(gam_features, final_training_keep)
final_gam_prep <- fit_preprocessor(
  x_raw[final_gam_features],
  scale = FALSE
)
final_gam_x <- apply_preprocessor(
  final_gam_prep,
  x_raw[final_gam_features]
)
final_gam_formula <- make_gam_formula(
  intersect(gam_continuous, names(final_gam_x)),
  intersect(gam_linear, names(final_gam_x))
)
final_gam_fit <- mgcv::gam(
  final_gam_formula,
  data = data.frame(outcome = y, final_gam_x, check.names = FALSE),
  family = binomial(),
  method = "REML",
  select = TRUE
)

effect_variables <- intersect(c("Age", "HR_mean", "Temp_mean"), gam_continuous)

make_effect_data <- function(variable) {
  base_values <- vapply(final_gam_x, median, numeric(1))
  grid <- seq(
    quantile(final_gam_x[[variable]], 0.05),
    quantile(final_gam_x[[variable]], 0.95),
    length.out = 100
  )
  newdata <- as.data.frame(matrix(
    rep(base_values, each = length(grid)),
    nrow = length(grid),
    dimnames = list(NULL, names(base_values))
  ))
  newdata[[variable]] <- grid
  term_prediction <- predict(
    final_gam_fit,
    newdata = newdata,
    type = "terms",
    se.fit = TRUE
  )
  term_name <- grep(
    paste0("^s\\(", variable, "\\)"),
    colnames(term_prediction$fit),
    value = TRUE
  )[[1]]
  tibble(
    predictor = variable,
    value = grid,
    centered_log_odds = term_prediction$fit[, term_name],
    se = term_prediction$se.fit[, term_name],
    lower = centered_log_odds - 1.96 * se,
    upper = centered_log_odds + 1.96 * se
  )
}

gam_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(effect_variables, make_effect_data))

gam_edf <- as.data.frame(summary(final_gam_fit)$s.table) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("term") |>
  transmute(
    term,
    edf = edf,
    p_value = `p-value`
  )

effect_edf <- function(variable) {
  row <- gam_edf[grepl(paste0("^s\\(", variable, "\\)"), gam_edf$term), ]
  if (nrow(row) == 0L) return(NA_real_)
  row$edf[[1]]
}

shape_label <- function(variable) {
  e <- gam_effects |> filter(predictor == variable)
  low <- e$centered_log_odds[[1]]
  mid <- e$centered_log_odds[[ceiling(nrow(e) / 2)]]
  high <- e$centered_log_odds[[nrow(e)]]
  if (low > mid && high > mid) return("a U-shaped pattern")
  if (low < mid && high < mid) return("an inverted-U pattern")
  if (high > low) return("an overall increasing pattern")
  "an overall decreasing pattern"
}
```

```{r}
#| label: gam-partial-effects
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "Centered GAM smooths on the log-odds scale. Bands are approximate 95% confidence intervals; other predictors are held at their medians."

effect_labels <- c(
  Age = "Age (years)",
  HR_mean = "Mean heart rate",
  Temp_mean = "Mean temperature"
)

ggplot(gam_effects, aes(x = value, y = centered_log_odds)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), fill = "#7AA6C2", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(color = "#235A7C", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey45") +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ predictor,
    scales = "free_x",
    labeller = as_labeller(effect_labels)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Centered contribution to log odds of death",
    title = "Selected non-linear effects in the final GAM"
  )
```

Age has an effective degrees of freedom (EDF) of
`r sprintf('%.2f', effect_edf('Age'))` and shows
`r shape_label('Age')`. Its EDF is close to one, so the effect is approximately
linear; increasing risk with age is clinically plausible because physiologic
reserve generally declines. Mean heart rate has EDF
`r sprintf('%.2f', effect_edf('HR_mean'))` and shows
`r shape_label('HR_mean')`. The modest curvature and overall increase are
clinically plausible because tachycardia can mark physiologic stress, although
the fitted curve does not show a strong separate rise at the bradycardic end.
Mean temperature has EDF `r sprintf('%.2f', effect_edf('Temp_mean'))` and shows
`r shape_label('Temp_mean')`. This is meaningfully non-linear; higher risk at
the low-temperature end is clinically plausible in severe illness, while the
expected high-fever upturn is not strongly supported over the central 90% of
observed values. These statements describe predictive patterns and do not imply
causal effects.

# 2.7 Model comparison and final choice

```{r}
#| label: comparison-tables

model_order <- c("LASSO", "GAM", "RandomForest", "SAPS_I", "SOFA")

comparison_summary <- fold_metrics |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = model_order)) |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarise(
    mean_AUROC = mean(AUROC),
    sd_AUROC = sd(AUROC),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_AUROC))

comparison_table <- fold_metrics |>
  mutate(
    model = factor(model, levels = model_order),
    Fold = paste0("Fold ", fold),
    AUROC = round(AUROC, 3)
  ) |>
  select(model, Fold, AUROC) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Fold, values_from = AUROC) |>
  left_join(
    comparison_summary |>
      mutate(
        mean_AUROC = round(mean_AUROC, 3),
        sd_AUROC = round(sd_AUROC, 3)
      ),
    by = "model"
  ) |>
  arrange(match(model, model_order))

knitr::kable(
  comparison_table,
  caption = "Outer-fold AUROC for the three models and two benchmark scores"
)
```

The comparison table places every method on the identical five held-out folds.
`r as.character(comparison_summary$model[[1]])` has the highest mean AUROC;
the standard deviations quantify how much discrimination varies across patient
splits rather than hiding that variation behind a single pooled estimate.

```{r}
#| label: oof-roc-curves
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Receiver operating characteristic curves from out-of-fold predictions. Every stay is scored by a model that was not trained on that stay."

roc_data <- oof_predictions |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(model_order),
    names_to = "model",
    values_to = "score"
  ) |>
  group_by(model) |>
  group_modify(~ {
    roc_object <- pROC::roc(
      .x$truth, .x$score,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      direction = "<",
      quiet = TRUE
    )
    coords <- pROC::coords(
      roc_object,
      x = "all",
      ret = c("specificity", "sensitivity"),
      transpose = FALSE
    )
    as_tibble(coords)
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = model_order))

ggplot(roc_data, aes(x = 1 - specificity, y = sensitivity, color = model)) +
  geom_path(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey55") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    x = "False-positive rate",
    y = "True-positive rate",
    color = "Model / score",
    title = "Out-of-fold ROC curves on set-a"
  )
```

The out-of-fold receiver operating characteristic curves show that the three
fitted models separate deaths from survivors substantially better than either
benchmark across most false-positive rates. Each curve uses predictions made
for stays that were excluded from the corresponding model fit.

```{r}
#| label: select-and-refit-final-model

candidate_summary <- comparison_summary |>
  filter(model %in% c("LASSO", "GAM", "RandomForest")) |>
  mutate(model = as.character(model))

best_model <- candidate_summary$model[[which.max(candidate_summary$mean_AUROC)]]
best_auc <- max(candidate_summary$mean_AUROC)
best_model_sd <- candidate_summary$sd_AUROC[[
  which.max(candidate_summary$mean_AUROC)
]]
lasso_auc <- candidate_summary$mean_AUROC[candidate_summary$model == "LASSO"]

benchmark_summary <- comparison_summary |>
  filter(model %in% c("SAPS_I", "SOFA")) |>
  mutate(model = as.character(model))
best_benchmark_row <- which.max(benchmark_summary$mean_AUROC)
best_benchmark_name <- benchmark_summary$model[[best_benchmark_row]]
best_benchmark_auc <- benchmark_summary$mean_AUROC[[best_benchmark_row]]
best_benchmark_sd <- benchmark_summary$sd_AUROC[[best_benchmark_row]]
benchmark_gap <- best_auc - best_benchmark_auc

final_model_name <- if (lasso_auc >= best_auc - 0.01) "LASSO" else best_model

# Refit random forest on all set-a so it is available if selected.
full_rf_inner <- make_stratified_folds(y, inner_k, seed = 77001)
final_rf_best <- tune_rf(x_raw, y, full_rf_inner, seed = 78001)
final_rf_prep <- fit_preprocessor(
  x_raw[final_training_keep],
  scale = FALSE
)
final_rf_x <- apply_preprocessor(
  final_rf_prep,
  x_raw[final_training_keep]
)
final_rf_fit <- fit_one_rf(
  final_rf_x, y,
  mtry = min(final_rf_best$mtry[[1]], ncol(final_rf_x)),
  min_node = final_rf_best$min.node.size[[1]],
  seed = 79001
)

final_object <- switch(
  final_model_name,
  LASSO = list(
    model_name = "LASSO",
    fit = final_lasso_fit,
    preprocessor = final_lasso_prep,
    lambda = final_lasso_tuning$lambda,
    predictor_columns = names(final_lasso_prep$medians),
    feature_threshold = rare_measurement_threshold,
    kept_parameters = kept_parameters
  ),
  GAM = list(
    model_name = "GAM",
    fit = final_gam_fit,
    preprocessor = final_gam_prep,
    gam_features = final_gam_features,
    predictor_columns = names(final_gam_prep$medians),
    feature_threshold = rare_measurement_threshold,
    kept_parameters = kept_parameters
  ),
  RandomForest = list(
    model_name = "RandomForest",
    fit = final_rf_fit,
    preprocessor = final_rf_prep,
    tuning = final_rf_best,
    predictor_columns = names(final_rf_prep$medians),
    feature_threshold = rare_measurement_threshold,
    kept_parameters = kept_parameters
  )
)

saveRDS(final_object, file.path(out_dir, "cp2_final_model.rds"))

stopifnot(
  file.exists(file.path(out_dir, "cp2_final_model.rds")),
  file.exists(file.path(out_dir, "cp2_oof_predictions.csv"))
)
```

The highest mean outer-fold AUROC among the three fitted models was
`r best_model` (`r sprintf('%.3f', best_auc)`). LASSO achieved
`r sprintf('%.3f', lasso_auc)`. I selected **`r final_model_name`** as the final
model: LASSO is preferred when it is within 0.01 AUROC of the best model because
its sparse standardized coefficients are substantially easier to inspect;
otherwise the empirically best model is retained. This rule was stated before
examining set-b or set-c, neither of which is read here.

The strongest benchmark was `r best_benchmark_name`, with mean AUROC
`r sprintf('%.3f', best_benchmark_auc)` and fold-to-fold standard deviation
`r sprintf('%.3f', best_benchmark_sd)`. The best fitted model exceeds it by
`r sprintf('%.3f', benchmark_gap)` AUROC. This gap is
**`r ifelse(benchmark_gap > max(best_model_sd, best_benchmark_sd), 'larger', 'not larger')`**
than the larger of the two fold-to-fold standard deviations
(`r sprintf('%.3f', max(best_model_sd, best_benchmark_sd))`). Therefore,
`r ifelse(benchmark_gap > max(best_model_sd, best_benchmark_sd),
  'the improvement over SAPS-I and SOFA is much larger than ordinary fold-to-fold variation in this analysis',
  'the apparent improvement is not clearly larger than ordinary fold-to-fold variation')`.
This supports a discrimination advantage on set-a, but it does not establish
clinical usefulness or external validity; those require Checkpoint 3.

# Output and reproducibility checks

```{r}
#| label: output-checks

required_outputs <- c(
  file.path(out_dir, "cp2_final_model.rds"),
  file.path(out_dir, "cp2_oof_predictions.csv")
)

stopifnot(
  all(file.exists(required_outputs)),
  all(file.info(required_outputs)$size > 0),
  nrow(oof_predictions) == expected_n,
  !anyDuplicated(oof_predictions$RecordID)
)

tibble(
  Output = basename(required_outputs),
  `Size (MB)` = round(file.info(required_outputs)$size / 1024^2, 2)
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Checkpoint 2 artifacts saved for Checkpoint 3")
```

The out-of-fold file contains one prediction per stay for all three models and
both benchmark scores. The saved final-model object contains the fitted model,
its training-derived preprocessing values, and the feature specification needed
to apply the same transformation in Checkpoint 3.
